| [CLAIM-146](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-146.md) | Recovering latent relational structure from an interaction matrix, with no privileged latent coordinates, is decades-old prior art, so the manuscript's contribution cannot be that recovery | The owner's prior-art objection at U58 to A207's closing framing, conceded by A210 in its first sentence and extended by A214 to identifiability and cross-lingual alignment. It does not hold for individual topics, which are recovered only by privileging the nonnegative representation, and uniquely only under separability or anchor-word conditions. | Active |
| [CLAIM-148](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-148.md) v4 | A matrix factorization is identified only up to an invertible change of latent coordinates, which weight decay narrows to rotations and nonnegativity to rescalings and permutations plus a data-dependent remainder; such a gauge is not a symmetry of the relational system, and automorphisms of the data act on the factors only when the factorization is identifiable | Drawn by the assistant at A207 §3, made explicit at A214 §6 and kept in A218 (§4.2, Ch5.4–5.9). It does not say latent axes are meaningless, or that observed data have non-trivial automorphisms. | Active |
| [CLAIM-149](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-149.md) v2 | A probe family that supplies a transformation's training signal cannot also certify what the transformation preserves: preservation must be shown under probes that were not used to train it | The owner set the frame at U51 ("a useful case study ... the projected GAN work"); A184 §§3–4 argued it, with its Experiment C and closing maxim, and A203 §30 and A218 Study 6 keep it. ([CASE-041](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-041.md)) is a documented instance, which the exchange did not know of. The documented support is one training case, in image generation, and one selection case, in translation (CASE-071). | Active |
| [CLAIM-150](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-150.md) v2 | An ontology of intrinsically individuated objects with relational properties can reproduce the categorical and operational identifications, and the predictions, of a relational one, so identification underdetermines constitution | The exchange's own guard, stated six times (A187, A191 §4, A198 §VI, A203 §35, A214 §13, A218 §13). That suits the non-eliminative choice and gives elimination no support. The ontological thesis needs its own conceptual argument; the mathematics and the experiments cannot supply it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) v6 | Any individuation built on sufficiency is relative to the target it is sufficient for: fix the outcomes differently and a different partition wins, so no boundary drawn this way is universal | Dual-filed from [MOM-POS-001](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/positions.d/POS-001.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). A sufficient statistic is sufficient for a target Y, so every partition chosen as minimal sufficient inherits Y. MOM's example: fix the outcomes differently and "organism" wins instead of "animal". In this record it is the standing caution on every boundary criterion filed beside it ([CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md), [CLAIM-161](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-161.md)). It does not say boundaries are arbitrary, only that each is relative to a stated target. | Active |
| [CLAIM-153](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md) | Failure of a self to hold together across contexts is a monodromy around a cycle of contexts: any two locally consistent contexts glue, and the minimal model of the obstruction needs three | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-165](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-165.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). Model contexts (roles, personas, sub-agents) as a cover, and the offsets that reconcile neighbours as a cochain. A global section, one coherent self, exists exactly when the monodromy Φ around a cycle vanishes. Two contexts always glue, so compartmentalization needs a loop. The frustrated XY or Kuramoto energy finds the obstruction: its minimum is 0 exactly when Φ ≡ 0. Abelian case only; re-checked here. | Active |
| [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) v3 | A candidate structure is worth naming as a unit when its effect-to-noise ratio outruns the Occam cost of keeping it: reify when d'² exceeds the log prior-to-posterior variance ratio, where the model with the candidate stays regular at the parameters that switch it off | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-160](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-160.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). By the Savage–Dickey ratio, ln BF(keep) = ½(d'² − Occam), so a direction, block or sector is real enough to name exactly when δ/ε > τ with τ² = ln(s²/σ²), the information the data added about it. In this record it prices the boundary tests for a combined form: a near-decomposable block ([LIT-905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-905.md)) earns a name when its gap beats its Occam factor. Re-checked here in the conjugate case. Narrowed to candidates whose model stays regular where they are switched off; where it is singular the rule overcharges (CLAIM-188). | Active |
| [CLAIM-159](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-159.md) v3 | The record's rival accounts of will are claims about drive profiles in different cells: Ainslie's interests are aggregate or emergent, the expected value of control is top-down, and will-organization is the maintained organization that governs how the drive profile changes | The assistant's reading, offered in chat on 2026-10-11 and filed at the owner's prompt. Ainslie's will has no governor: the person is "just the resultant" of bargaining interests, which is aggregate, or emergent if resolve is a property only the recursion has. The expected value of control posits a dedicated specifying system, which is top-down. The will paper's will-organization is the maintained organization of relations that decides which regime is effective, so it governs the drive profile's changes over time. That is the owner's point that "who drives" is not constant. | Active |
| [CLAIM-164](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-164.md) v4 | What a spectral gap makes definite is the subspace of the cluster it isolates, not a single direction: the gap picks the object, and the object is a vector only when its own gap is wide | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-144](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-144.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). Under a perturbation δT, the subspace spanned by a cluster of singular values separated by a gap δ rotates by at most ‖δT‖/δ (Davis–Kahan), whatever happens to the vectors inside it. So the well-defined unit is the gap-isolated projector. Re-measured here. With [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) it is a criterion: the gap picks the object, and the Occam factor says whether the gap is big enough. | Active |
| [CLAIM-172](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md) v10 | Mutual entrainment is a sufficient mark of a combined form, and marks it as one of peers: when each side adjusts the other's timing the pair carries a collective variable neither has alone; one-way drive also makes a combined form, with a hierarchical architecture | The record's reading in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11, "connect extended self to entrainment". Clark & Chalmers' marks of extension are availability marks, and the coupling-constitution objection says coupling does not entail parthood. Mutual entrainment sidesteps the objection rather than answering it: it individuates a new system by its collective variable. It does not cover a passive store like Otto's notebook, which is coupled across time by writing and reading, not by timing. | Active |
| [CLAIM-175](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-175.md) v3 | A partner-dancing couple, while dancing, is one combined cognitive form on the extended-mind thesis's own terms, more clearly than Otto and his notebook, and merits a name of its own | The owner's reply of 2026-10-11 to the dancers objection, which they had not read: "under extended mind thesis, I'd argue that the pair, while dancing together, comprises a combined form that merits some privileged nomenclature of some kind". So the objection fails against the combined form and survives only as a question about selfhood. The name is not yet chosen. | Active |
| [CLAIM-177](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) v3 | In the record's exchanges with collaborators who keep no memory, the argument repeatedly loses identity: concepts are redefined silently, objections and readings come back as though new, and the thesis changes without anyone arguing for the change | Stated as a finding in [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md), from seven readers coding the will exchange, and found again in the What Survives Translation? exchange by the workbench reconstructions of 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10. Filed on 2026-10-11 as the first premise of the manuscript. Active since version 2 (2026-10-27), when the body counted six exchanges; the general form beyond one owner and one assistant family is CLAIM-483, Proposed. | Active |
| [CLAIM-188](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-188.md) v4 | Where the model with a candidate structure is singular at the parameters that switch the candidate off, with real log canonical threshold λ below d/2 and multiplicity m, the reification rule's Gaussian Occam term overcharges keeping the candidate by (d/2 − λ) log n + (m − 1) log log n to leading order, so near the threshold the rule prunes candidates the Bayes factor keeps, and its derivation holds only where that model stays regular | A narrowing of [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md), filed on 2026-10-11 from a synthesis review that found the record already held the readings that limit it. [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md)'s rule prices a candidate with a Gaussian Occam factor, which is exact in the conjugate case it was re-checked in. The candidates it is meant for (blocks, sectors, couplings with hidden structure) are often singular where they are switched off. There THEORY-087 puts the penalty at λ log n − (m − 1) log log n, not (d/2) log n. On CASE-152's product model the rule prunes, near the threshold, candidates the exact Bayes factor keeps. CLAIM-154 is narrowed to models that stay regular at the switch-off. | Active |
| [CLAIM-194](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md) v4 | A gap or coupling criterion cannot tell a boundary a system produces from one imposed on it: a membrane the cell makes and a beam joining two pendulums pass alike, so the block test cannot by itself supply the individuality minimal agency needs | A counter to the block criterion and to the agency test's first condition, found by two separate reviews of the unlinked THEORYs in the third synthesis pass. [THEORY-072](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-072.md) and THEORY-1119 place the line at production and self-distinction instead. No case has been measured: the point is that a coupling statistic has no term for who made the coupling. | Active |
| [CLAIM-195](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-195.md) v2 | For an argument, the constraint set that persistence is relative to is fixed by an amendable decision, not discovered: the record stipulates what counts as the same claim persisting, which makes the choice explicit without making it non-arbitrary | Files the point the workbench of 2026-10-11 (214308) left as notes on [CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) and [CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md). That shows how one system fixes its set; it does not show the choice is non-arbitrary. | Active |
| [CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md) | Sections over contexts that do not overlap always glue, so a sense that differs between disjoint contexts is not a gluing failure: a failure needs an overlap carrying sections that disagree, and which families count as covers decides whether anything glues | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-088](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-088.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). The sheaf condition says a family of sections that agree on overlaps glues to one global section. Where two contexts do not overlap, agreement is vacuous and they glue. So "tall", which takes one threshold for people and another for trees, is one global section with the comparison class part of the meaning, not a failure of gluing. A failure needs contexts that overlap and carry sections that disagree there. Which families count as covering is the piece that decides whether anything glues, and a sheaf picture of meaning that does not state it has decided nothing. | Active |
| [CLAIM-199](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md) v3 | Blackwell's order bounds what a rendering makes possible for any receiver, and a given receiver's access is usable information relative to the rules it can apply, which a garbling can raise for that receiver but never above what the source makes possible | The record's reconciliation, on 2026-10-10, of [CLAIM-225](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-225.md). Both standards are kept, in different roles: Blackwell's order is the ceiling, and [TERM-034](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-034.md)'s interpreter-relative fidelity ("relative to an interpreter and its available side information") is the receiver's. [CLAIM-087](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-087.md)'s improvement is a gain in usable information. The nearest held reading is [THEORY-176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-176.md)'s "Its loss bounds r's best attainable risk for that problem from above", for restricted rules. The example is checkable; whether real receivers show such gains is a proposal. The usable-information literature was not held when it was filed; Xu et al.'s V-information is now read (note of 2026-10-21). It does not say which rule class real readers have. | Active |
| [CLAIM-205](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-205.md) v3 | Functional and relevance-theoretic accounts of translation, as Nida, Nord and Gutt state them, need not fix one context or a static stance profile of the rendering | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12. Narrowed and promoted on 2026-10-30, when Nida, Nord and Gutt were read; the baseline it proposed is CLAIM-504. | Active |
| [CLAIM-207](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md) | The transports of Propositions 1–2 and of D_obs act on judgement outcomes, not texts, and for any one source–target pair a constant kernel transports any overlap-consistent target, so they constrain a translation only once one kernel family is fixed across many utterances and derived from the text channel | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. It does not say [CLAIM-121](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-121.md) or [CLAIM-070](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-070.md) is false; it bears on what they are used to support. | Active |
| [CLAIM-208](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-208.md) v2 | The compositional predictions are upper bounds whose constants cannot be estimated from serial-reproduction data in a metric fixed beforehand, so the compositional half of the success criterion cannot fail | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The recursion e_n ≤ (∏κ_j)e_0 + Σε_i∏κ_j is a theorem once its constants are the true ones, so a chain cannot depart from it; it can only show a constant was misestimated. A sensitivity κ_i belongs to a reteller's kernel and needs many retellings of each of several inputs at every generation, where a chain gives one. And [CLAIM-059](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-059.md) says amplification "needs a metric other than total variation" (now held as CLAIM-267), so the regime depends on a metric chosen afterwards. [CLAIM-078](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-078.md) records that the compositional half was dropped from the manuscript, not that it cannot fail as stated. It does not say error propagation is unimportant. | Active |
| [CLAIM-210](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-210.md) v2 | Sharing a kind and being a rendering are different relations: kind-sharing is symmetric and says what is to be preserved, while fidelity belongs to a transport from a given source, so an utterance of the same kind made independently of the source shares its kind and has no fidelity to it | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-246](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-246.md). The October thesis puts fidelity in what persists "through those transformations", and [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md) makes fidelity the distortion profile of a transport. So the objection's independent utterance I shares the source's kind and has no fidelity to it, since no transport relates them; the translation T has both. T's provenance is a fact the transport clause supplies, not something the kind criterion must recover. [CLAIM-002](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)'s continuity of transmission concerns the identity of a work, which [TERM-040](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-040.md) keeps apart from the kind. Active, because it is read off the record's own texts. It does not say judges track descent. | Active |

[CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md) shows that the receiver's test and the analyst's identifiability come apart in both directions, and stops at "It does not say the October thesis is false". On those cases [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) and [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s fidelity clause give opposite verdicts on what survived, yet the two are joined by `complements`, which says they answer different parts of one question and do not compete, and [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) answers only [QUESTION-029](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-029.md). Granted: it is a comparison of texts and of the record's relations. It does not say which criterion is right. | Active |
| [CLAIM-214](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-214.md) v2 | The distribution-over-situations criterion compares each language's own listener posterior, so it needs no correspondence of alternative sets; that a literal rendering can fail it is the criterion detecting a lost implicature, and a target language may admit no rendering that passes | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-236](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-236.md). On the rational-speech-act model each posterior is computed with its own language's alternatives, so comparing the posteriors needs no map between the alternative sets. Active, because it is read off the criterion's form and checked by arithmetic. It does not say the model is right or that the criterion applies to poems. | Active |
| [CLAIM-216](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-216.md) v2 | A thesis that conjoins relational constitution, statistical recovery, transport and receivers' recovery is defeated whole by any one of its empirical findings, though its clauses can hold or fail apart, so the line is better put as separate theses, each with its own defeat condition, resting on one another only where one is a premise of another | The interlocutor's objection at U62 (A240) to the October thesis ([CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)) and to the record's restatement of it ([CLAIM-204](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md)), given as the reason for superseding [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md): "Separates ontology, statistical recovery, and empirical transport instead of making them rise or fall together". Active since 2026-10-30; CLAIM-204 concedes it. It says what would answer it, and does not say an integrative statement is useless. | Active |
| [CLAIM-218](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-218.md) | The task-paired risk difference the record uses in place of Blackwell's order, D_Q = sup_q \|R_q(U) − R_τ(q)(V)\|, is a different quantity: it reduces each risk set to one number, needs the losses of paired tasks on one scale, and its absolute value counts improvement as distortion | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md) is stated in Blackwell's order, and the record's decision term is A86's D_Q. A risk per task needs a prior or a minimax summary, where Blackwell's order compares whole risk sets. Subtracting the risks of two tasks needs their losses on one scale, which nothing supplies. The absolute value makes D_Q symmetric, against [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md). Granted, because each point is elementary. It objects to [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md) by undermining the measure meant to realize it, not [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)'s truth, and it does not say a decision term is unworkable. | Active |
| [CLAIM-219](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-219.md) v4 | A change in the global compatibility of a fixed scenario is either a change in contextuality proper, which the behavioural data read show none of, or a change in overlap consistency, which is ordinary context dependence and moves by at most 2ε when each context moves by ε | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The only instance of the headline is the stipulated [CASE-037](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-037.md). Among the claims [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md) is cited only by [CLAIM-041](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-041.md), not by [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md). The objection is open; it does not say a contextual pragmatic data set cannot exist. | Active |
| [CLAIM-222](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md) v2 | No design in the programme includes an interlingual translation, and the defeat conditions are disjunctive, so English retellings and model chains could settle a thesis about what survives translation | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens). | [CLAIM-223](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-223.md) v2 | Whether a distinction survived is fixed by what the receivers can recover, and whether it can be shown to have survived is fixed by what the analyst's probes can identify, so the manuscript's thesis and the October fidelity clause, read so, answer different parts of one question | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-211](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-211.md), and the argument [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md) asked for: "the thesis now needs both conditions, or an argument for dropping one". On [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md)'s cases: a distinction identifiable but unusable did not survive for those receivers; one usable but unidentifiable survived without evidence of it. | [CLAIM-225](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-225.md) v4 | Blackwell's order measures what an ideal decision-maker could do, not what a given receiver can reconstruct, and the line's claims that a rendering can improve access describe garblings that real receivers do better with, which is the shape of the Blackwell thesis's own defeat condition | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange connects the two claims. It is distinct from [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md), which sets the analyst against the receiver: this sets the ideal receiver against an actual one. | Active |
| [CLAIM-226](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md) v2 | The defeat tests pool unnamed judges and treat their disagreement as noise, though the theory makes the act partly constituted by its audience; for historical sources there is no source audience at all, and for interlingual ones population differences are read as distortion | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it.
