| [CLAIM-360](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-360.md) v2 | The deep-versus-shallow learning results separate three effects that aggregate loss conflates: a larger realizable function class, a larger set reachable within a fixed data and compute budget, and a different internal organization with the same attainable outcomes; the deep linear results show the third, the random-hierarchy results the second, and the depth-separation result for products of inputs the first, at fixed size | The owner's, U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A37's proposed experiment: "I think we may already have an empirical demonstration that would be useful here in the wide vs deep literature." | [CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md) v3 | On a norm-ball update set the local frustration residual Φ_r = min over ‖d‖ ≤ r of max_i(ε_i + g_iᵀd) equals the maximum over the simplex of Σλ_iε_i − r‖Σλ_ig_i‖_*, so infeasibility of the declared improvements has a certificate, and any admissible actual update exceeds Φ_r by a nonnegative governance regret | A34 §4 and A35 §3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, checked. The residual is the smallest worst-case shortfall of the declared local improvements ε_i over updates of size at most r. Minimax for the bilinear problem on two compact convex sets gives the dual over the simplex, so Φ_r > 0 exactly when some λ certifies that no update meets all demands (A34's form). Governance regret Γ is the gap between an actual admissible update's shortfall and Φ_r, and is never negative. For L₁ = (θ − 1)², L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0, Φ_r = ε for every r. The sharp edge: per A37 it is a cardinal refinement of the ordinal fact ([CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)), and its magnitude depends on units (A36 §2D). | Active |
| [CLAIM-366](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md) v3 | Whether several objectives share a strict first-order descent direction, 0 ∉ conv{g_i}, is invariant under smooth invertible reparameterization, while the sign of a Euclidean gradient inner product is not, and a negative inner product does not exclude common descent; a budgeted version is invariant only with the metric pulled back | A35 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, at the owner's U35 "double click" on whether functionally equivalent parameterizations give equivalent frustration diagnoses. The practice corollary, not to diagnose task conflict by gradient cosine, is the anthology's. | Active |
| [CLAIM-368](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-368.md) v6 | The primitive for an organization's regulatory difficulty is frustration, not distress: a relation between maintained, consequential demands and the incompatibilities, constraints or countervailing processes that limit their realization, independent of strain, the burden of sustaining activity, and distinct from distress, a possible integrated response to either | The owner's, U33 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "maybe we should focus less on distress and more on frustration". | [CLAIM-369](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-369.md) v2 | In symmetric resource-mediated competition with interaction matrix A = UᵀU and growth rates r = Uᵀb − c, Lotka–Volterra population dynamics are multiplicative gradient flow on the convex feature-selection objective ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn over the nonnegative orthant: the invasion fitness of an absent component is the negative partial derivative of that objective, and the uninvadable equilibria are its KKT points | From a synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18 (workbench entry of that date), checked here and given a proof. When competition between components is mediated by shared resources with feature or niche vectors u_i, so that A = UᵀU and r = Uᵀb − c, the Lotka–Volterra dynamics are ṅ_i = −n_i ∂_i L with L(n) = ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn: entropic mirror descent on the positive orthant. A rare component's invasion fitness is −∂_i L, the value of adding that feature, and uninvadable equilibria are the KKT points of the convex program. The sharp edge: the identity needs a shared scalar objective, and it fails for asymmetric interactions or processes with competing objectives, which is where an organization stops being an optimizer. | [CLAIM-370](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-370.md) | For a symmetric positive-pair distribution with marginal p, the conditional-expectation operator on L²(p) has the density ratio K⁺ as its kernel, and it is Hilbert–Schmidt exactly when the χ²-divergence of the pair from the product of its marginals is finite, in which case it is compact and self-adjoint with an orthonormal eigenbasis | [THEORY-005](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-005.md)'s derivation, stated as the record's own and with its proof. Here the condition is exact: Hilbert–Schmidt if and only if finite χ². It says nothing about what trained features span. | Active |

| [CLAIM-372](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-372.md) | Within a fixed measurement scenario, the contextual fraction is a piecewise-linear and Lipschitz-continuous function of the empirical model's probability table, with a constant that depends only on the scenario | The record's own derivation, from the linear programme of Abramsky, Barbosa and Mansfield ([LIT-265](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-265.md), Eq. 3), which [THEORY-165](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-165.md) holds. | [CLAIM-373](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-373.md) | If a map approximately intertwines two operators, with defects E_A = ΦA − A′Φ and E_B = ΦB − B′Φ, then Φ[A,B] − [A′,B′]Φ = A′E_B + E_A B − B′E_A − E_B A, so the commutator is carried to within (‖A‖ + ‖A′‖)‖E_B‖ + (‖B‖ + ‖B′‖)‖E_A‖ | The commutator-distortion identity of the manuscript's §9, on its own and proved. | [CLAIM-374](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-374.md) | On a consistently connected system, Contextuality-by-Default and the sheaf criterion agree: a maximally connected coupling exists exactly when a global law has the contexts' laws as its marginals | The record's derivation of what [NOTE-600](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-600.md) marks as its own inference. | [CLAIM-375](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-375.md) v2 | Under one-hop allocation within an epoch, an operator that grants influence to an ally whose policy is nearer its own than the collective decision is raises how far its preferred policy is realized while its own authority stays fixed, so the two conditions of the grant scheme hold together | The demonstrated core of [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md). | [CLAIM-376](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-376.md) | A linear system that is stable at every instant can have a positive Lyapunov exponent: shifting any operator with exponent λ > 0 by −δI lowers its exponent by exactly δ and makes every instantaneous operator stable, so for 0 < δ < λ the shifted system is stable at every instant and unstable | The case [THEORY-724](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-724.md)'s source asserts and does not show. | [CLAIM-377](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-377.md) | For any differentiable model under squared loss with Gaussian noise of precision β, the model's Fisher on n inputs is the Gauss–Newton matrix βJᵀJ, and its non-zero eigenvalues are exactly β times those of the empirical NTK Gram matrix JJᵀ, with the same multiplicities, its eigenvectors being Jᵀ applied to the Gram matrix's, normalized | [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md)'s Step 1, stated as the record's own and proved. | [CLAIM-378](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-378.md) | A representational similarity index invariant to every invertible linear map depends on a representation only through its column space, so it takes one value on all column-centred representations of rank n − 1, as it does on all representations of rank n | The generalization of [THEORY-236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md)'s theorem. | [CLAIM-380](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-380.md) v2 | With finitely many states and finitely many outcomes, the positive part of the Bayes-risk increase on the same decision problem is directed, is zero from a garbling back to its source, vanishes for every finite problem and prior exactly when the rendering is at least as informative as the source, and has A86's D_Q as its symmetrization | The finite-outcome part of [CLAIM-326](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-326.md). | [CLAIM-381](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-381.md) | Over a finite class of items with finite judgement outcomes, a constant outcome kernel fits every item only when the target readers' averaged responses do not vary with the item, an exact fit is a garbling with the item as common parameter, and Le Cam's deficiency and its restriction to finitely many decision problems are finite computations | The derivational core of [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md). | [CLAIM-382](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-382.md) | In an autoencoder initialised with i.i.d. Gaussian weights and zero biases and trained by SGD or momentum SGD on a loss of its output, the law of each hidden layer's learned representation is invariant under every orthogonal map of that layer that commutes with its activation, so under a radial activation no basis is privileged in law, while elementwise tanh or Leaky-ReLU yields invariance only under the signed permutations or the permutations, which leaves the standard axes free to be privileged | [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s symmetry argument, stated as the record's own and proved. | [CLAIM-383](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-383.md) | In plane Couette and plane Poiseuille flow, measured in the energy norm, the linearized operator about the laminar profile has transient growth at least cR and resolvent norm at least cR² with c independent of R, so wherever it is eigenvalue-stable a perturbation of norm at most CR⁻² makes it eigenvalue-unstable | [THEORY-304](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-304.md)'s scalings as lower bounds, derived. At streamwise wavenumber zero, the cross-stream velocities obey an R-independent Stokes problem in the time t/R. They force the streamwise velocity through −U′v, so the streamwise response is R times an R-independent field. In the energy norm this gives transient growth at least cR, and in the steady forced problem a resolvent norm at least cR². Through pseudospectra, a perturbation of norm O(R⁻²) then moves an eigenvalue into the unstable half-plane wherever the flow is eigenvalue-stable. | [CLAIM-385](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-385.md) v2 | If a symmetric operator on ℝⁿ commutes with an orthogonal representation of a compact group, each eigenspace is a sum of real irreducibles and each multiplicity a sum of multiples of their dimensions, so SO(2) and ℤ/n for n ≥ 3 force paired eigenvalues; conversely the spectrum fixes neither the group nor a basis inside an eigenspace |  | Active |

| [CLAIM-387](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-387.md) | Optimal deterministic information-bottleneck partitions at two budgets need not be nested: with X uniform on four states and binary Y with P(Y=1\|x) = (0, 0, 1/8, 3/8), the optimum is {0,1,2 \| 3} for 6.91 < β < 9.26 and {0,1 \| 2,3} for 9.26 < β < 16.06, two partitions neither of which refines the other | Found by brute force in the reading of Equitz and Cover ([NOTE-988](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-988.md)) and re-run here from scratch. | [CLAIM-388](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-388.md) v3 | Exact dynamical closure of a collective variable does not require a nearly decomposable block: in a linear Gaussian VAR(1) with uniform coupling among n units, the sum of all units is exactly dynamically independent at every stable coupling strength, while every partition of the units into two or more groups couples as strongly across its edges as within them | From A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-19 on coarse-to-fine processes, which gave the two-unit continuous-time case (ż = (b − a)z for z = x₁ + x₂) and the boxed slogan "Exact aggregation ⇏ near-decomposability". | [CLAIM-389](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-389.md) v2 | In a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1), exact dynamical independence of a linear coarse-graining implies that its Mori–Zwanzig memory vanishes, but not conversely: memory needs coupling out of the coarse variable and back, and dependence needs only the way back, so a coarse variable can be Markov in its own law with zero memory and still be dynamically dependent | Derived in the reading of Chorin, Hald and Kupferman (2000), [NOTE-989](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-989.md), and re-checked here. | [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md) | Under Montévil and Mossio's definition of closure, a closed set of constraints has at least two members, and if each constraint is produced at the time scale of a constraint in the set that generates it and not at the scale at which it is itself conserved, the set includes at least one slow and one fast dependence, so a system with a single constraint of its own cannot realise closure |  | Active |

| [CLAIM-399](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-399.md) | Causal abstraction in the senses of Rubenstein et al., Beckers and Halpern, and Beckers, Eberhardt and Halpern does not secure governance-response sufficiency: exact transformation, τ-abstraction and zero approximate-abstraction distance all accept the hidden-bit coarse-graining, which loses ρ(h = 1) bits of the response to h, because each lets high-level noise carry what the coarse state drops; for one outcome and the identity correspondence, sufficiency is their compatibility condition with the high-level context fixed to the coarse state, and strong abstraction rejects the case only through interventions on the hidden parameter | The record's join, on 2026-10-21, of its readings of the causal-abstraction papers ([NOTE-1037](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1037.md), [NOTE-1032](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1032.md), [NOTE-1045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1045.md)) with [CLAIM-407](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md). | [CLAIM-400](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-400.md) v4 | In the meaning–authority model linearized at symmetry, a third, maintained legibility state that authority moves (ε) and that moves interpretation (ν) or conferral (μ), with persistence λ < 1 and nonnegative couplings, destabilizes the symmetric state exactly when the two-variable condition holds with β + νε/(1 − λ) in place of β and δ + με/(1 − λ) in place of δ: at the threshold the regime is indistinguishable from stronger two-variable couplings, and the slower it is the more it adds, while away from the threshold it adds a mode that no two-variable model has, so a lean in the regime can outlast the advantages it was built from | [QUESTION-253](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-253.md) asked whether authority's effect on what becomes legible as evidence is a third channel with its own instability condition, or [CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md)'s κ′ renamed. Both, in different respects. With a maintained legibility state r, det(I − J₃) = (1 − λ)[(1 − α)(1 − δ) − βγ] − ε[νγ + μ(1 − α)], which is (1 − λ) times [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md)'s expression with β_eff = β + νε/(1 − λ) and δ_eff = δ + με/(1 − λ). So the instability threshold is a two-variable one with stronger couplings, and a slower regime (λ near 1) adds more. Away from the threshold, r is a third mode: a lean in the regime can hold interpretation and authority off symmetry after they would have relaxed, which no two-variable parameters reproduce. | Active |
| [CLAIM-401](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md) v4 | The conditions an effective description is commonly asked to meet are not of one kind: predictive sufficiency and approximation fidelity are adequacy relative to a declared target, metric and horizon; tractability restricts the operations under which adequacy is assessed; dynamical independence and memory closure are relations of the representation to the system, memory relative to a chosen projection; so a matrix over them as independent binary axes conflates kinds | A4 and A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U4 ("it sounds like considering it from this angle has potentially already altered our characterization of those 'virtues'"). | [CLAIM-402](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-402.md) v5 | Predictive success of a category across contexts warrants treating it as a real effective kind only when the evidence in those contexts does not pass through the category's own use, or when the effect of that use is modelled: a category that speakers or institutions act on can produce the regularities that confirm it, and contexts that share its use are not independent | A27 §1 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U27 ("are we perhaps better positioned now to address [QUESTION-007](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-007.md)? -009? -011? -028?"), after A26 §2's performative toy. | [CLAIM-403](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-403.md) v5 | A contribution's admission to an organization's inquiry, its recognition in apt terms, its credibility, its uptake into judgements, and its contributor's part in revising the standards of uptake are separable, each possible without the later ones, so an organization can widen access while every channel by which a less authoritative contribution could change the criteria of authority stays closed | A24 §6 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U24: "Someone's contribution may be received and politely acknowledged yet have no mechanism through which it can change institutional understanding." | [CLAIM-404](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md) v6 | An organization can be governed from outside without any of its decisions being made for it, through the evidence its own procedures receive or through the criteria by which they weigh evidence; the two routes are distinct and each is possible without the other, so informational and evaluative independence do not imply each other; and where the organization's role is to evaluate another that affects its evidence or resources, the interpretation–authority loop can close between the two institutions, so that formal independence of the evaluator's procedure does not make its evaluation independent | The owner's cases, U20 ("maybe cases like reflexive control and regulatory capture could be informative here") and U21 (news-media capture) of the exchange of 2026-10-20, with A26 §4's two constructions and A27 §6. | [CLAIM-405](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md) v2 | An individuation is well defined only once its criterion is fixed (the target it serves, the transformations its unity must survive, the scale), and that dependence does not make it arbitrary: once the criterion is fixed a verdict can be false, and differently fixed criteria can pick out units of one system whose boundaries cross rather than nest, none of them less real for it | The individuation counterpart of the owner's normative thesis [CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md) ("once they are fixed, the judgment can be false"), as A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-20 put it, on the owner's U8 question about "contextuality/relativity/subjectivity". | [CLAIM-408](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-408.md) v3 | In ḋ = (α − κ)d − βd³, with d the difference between two parties' shares of authority, α their self-reinforcement and κ a constraint that bears on both alike, the equal allocation is the only equilibrium and is stable for κ > α, and for κ < α it is unstable and the unequal allocations ±√((α − κ)/β) are stable: a constraint that favours neither party can, by weakening, destabilize the equal allocation and make persistent unequal allocations stable, of any size near the threshold (\|d*\| → 0 as κ → α), without determining which party gains the larger share, and in this model restoring κ > α restores the equal allocation | A19 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U19: does the account "capture 'deregulation' as a disguised effort to induce organizational symmetry breaking?" | [CLAIM-409](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-409.md) v2 | For one state law, one intervention distribution and one outcome, a deficiency of sufficiency cannot increase under refinement: if T₁ = g∘T₂ then Γ(T₂) ≤ Γ(T₁); informational closure, by contrast, is monotone in neither direction, since in the three-bit chain of Rosas et al. | [CLAIM-410](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-410.md) v5 | Removing a constraint on an organization's members does not move it along one scale of more or less governance: it changes a profile of who holds governing positions, among them rule-making, monitoring, enforcement, appeal and revision, in which the authority the constraint held can be eliminated, distributed or transferred, and the members' first-order options and their share in revising the conditions of their action can move in opposite directions | The owner's question, U18 of the exchange of 2026-10-20: "what does this suggest about e.g. "deregulation" as an ideological end?" | [CLAIM-411](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-411.md) v5 | Under the broad, nonphenomenal definition of interpretation the constitutive thesis uses, substantial processing that is not independently shown to be experiential meets the definition, blindsight's apparently unconscious visual discrimination among it, so interpretation alone does not establish experience, and the thesis must say which further organizational properties, if any, make an interpretation experiential | A3's "most serious challenge" to the owner's thesis, which every later reply accepted. | [CLAIM-413](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-413.md) v3 | Grounding is not a property of an experience but a relation among an interpretation, what it purports to be about, and a process that constrains it independently; its current, developmental and epistemic senses come apart from one another, and in the current sense it comes apart from whether the interpretation occurs, so ungrounded is not unconstrained, and what makes an interpretive organization experiential need not be what makes its contents veridical | The owner's premise at U1, that sensory apparatus is necessary for grounded experience, as A1, A3, A5 and A7 restated it. | [CLAIM-414](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md) v4 | Matched ordinary trajectories can conceal differences in an interpretation's efficacy, in the allocation of that efficacy, and in the maintenance of its enabling constraints: in two finite constructions, systems that agree under ordinary operation differ in each, and a specified intervention exposes the difference that passive observation of the matched trajectories does not | A10 of the exchange on experience and interpretation, re-run here. | [CLAIM-416](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-416.md) v4 | Competing perspectives compete over the tests that measure them as well as under them: success under an evaluative regime is evidence of competence relative to that regime, a fair test need not be neutral across competences, and a perspective that gains influence over the test can change what later success shows | From the owner's case at U35 of the exchange of 2026-10-22, rival schools of martial arts vying for dominance, and A35–A37's development of it. | [CLAIM-418](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-418.md) v3 | Possessing, enacting or being shaped by an organizational perspective does not establish an independent agent, and perspectival, agential and institutional boundaries need not coincide: several agents can share a perspective, one agent can act through several, and a perspective can be reproduced with no agent governing it; where a perspective contributes to an agent's activity it can enable and constrain the exercise of agency, and that exercise can reproduce or transform it, while whether agency universally requires such a perspective stays open | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the owner's question at U38, "what's the relationship between perspective and agency?", A38's answer, and A39's request that it be recorded. | [CLAIM-421](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-421.md) v4 | The cessation of an organizational perspective's enactment need not imply the loss of the dispositions, capacities or reproductive relationships from which it can be reinstated: an interruption can be of activation (the disposition is held but not engaged or retrievable), of enactment (held, but the material, institutional or social conditions for exercising it are gone) or of reproduction (held by some bearers, but the processes that pass it on are damaged), and temporary unavailability is not extinction, though prolonged interruption of reproduction can end a tradition | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22, at the owner's U37: the doorway effect as perspective meeting grounded experience, and the perspectival interruptions of the Chinese Cultural Revolution. | [CLAIM-434](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-434.md) | On a finite set of outcomes, some function rises with every move that wins one of a negotiation's conflicts exactly when no chain of winning moves returns to where it began, and the length of the longest such chain ending at an outcome is one such function; a perfectly transitive record of which side won each pair, in a complete tournament contesting every pair once, leaves a cyclic share of (n − 2)/3n under the Hodge decomposition, a baseline that does not carry to sparse records; the Hodge gradient can reverse a comparison the wins settle, netting a record erases alternation, a record fixes a class of potentials rather than one, a coherent record is not yet one aligned with any single perspective's ordering, a best-fitting ordering of a cycle is no Lyapunov function, the sign a class of potentials gives can be set-valued, and an ordering fitted to a record overstates its agreement there | The formal core of the rename of 2026-10-23 from "ascendancy" to "potential" ([TERM-076](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-076.md)). | [CLAIM-436](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-436.md) v4 | An instantaneous ordering is a common currency on a finite set of options, where every complete preorder has a real-valued representation, but not in general: the lexicographic order on the unit square has no real-valued representation, while a continuous complete preorder on a connected separable space has a continuous one; so admitting an ordering is strictly weaker than admitting a currency, a graded lexicographic override lies in the gap while an exact threshold override does not, a threshold override with a discrimination threshold is a lexicographic semiorder whose choices can cycle and so is no ordering at all, and even where each instant has a currency, successive currencies need not share exchange rates | The formal half of the owner's reframing of 2026-10-23, that a "common currency" is better read as a negotiation admitting an (at least instantaneous) ordering. | [CLAIM-469](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-469.md) v3 | Luria is an apparatus for a record's objects in the operational sense: through its schemes, vocabularies, validators and generated views it realizes a system of distinctions that fixes what counts as a referable and governable object within the record, so that a split scheme makes one object two and a promoted vocabulary makes a value an entity; it keeps, enforces and propagates those distinctions; and its distinctions are revised through the record's own use | The operational half of [CLAIM-476](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-476.md), split from it at the owner's review of the pull request. | [CLAIM-470](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-470.md) v4 | Inquiry is a form of specification: a question fixes which differences would count as an answer, an inquiry adds the operations that make those differences accessible, and what it finds can stabilize into a specification that constrains later inquiry; so inquiry stands to its findings as a specification to its realizations, with one difference, that an inquiry can revise what an answer could be | The owner's, U15 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "inquiry is a form of specification." | [CLAIM-475](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-475.md) v3 | Specifying is itself a resource-bounded realization: formulating a question takes time, concepts and computation as realizing a configuration takes energy and matter, so the questions an agent can ask are a product of what it has already realized; a stabilized specification is past inquiry stored so that later questions become cheaper to ask, and it can make other questions harder | The owner's, U17 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "resource constraints impact specification in exactly the same way as they impact realization. The relation's type is determinate where the relata's content is not, and that determinacy is no warrant for the dependency: [CLAIM-293](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-293.md) is the demonstrated case. [CASE-131](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-131.md) is the instance in which the rigidity of a relation outran what its relata meant and the grammar was amended. | Active |
| [CLAIM-480](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md) v2 | Composing interactions can turn an interior into a constraint, and sometimes into a constraint of a new kind: in the chain E = ½k₁(x₁ − x₂)² + ½k₂(x₂ − x₃)², with x₂ internal and equilibrated, the boundary sees E_eff = ½·k₁k₂/(k₁ + k₂)·(x₁ − x₃)², a coupling between x₁ and x₃ that neither part has; if the interior relaxes slowly, eliminating it leaves a history-dependent constraint, a memory kernel, so interconnection fixes an effective constraint on the boundary's trajectories and separation of time scales decides only whether that constraint is approximately memoryless; and for cellular sheaves the reduced constraint can relate three boundary values where every relation among the parts is pairwise | From A22 §4 and A23 §IV of the exchange of 2026-10-27, which called composition "the most important missing mechanism" after the owner's U20. Eliminating an equilibrated interior leaves an effective boundary relation that no part has; an outside system interacting only with the boundary meets it as a constraint, and "The interior has effectively become apparatus." Baez and Fong's black-boxing functor is the general theorem for passive linear networks. The memory case ties it to Mori–Zwanzig and to [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md): interconnection yields an effective constraint on the boundary's trajectories in every case, and separation of time scales decides only whether it is approximately memoryless. For cellular sheaves the reduction can need a richer relational vocabulary than the parts used (THEORY-1090; QUESTION-283). It is independent evidence for [CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md), that constraints are realized by organization. | Active |
| [CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md) | Coupling does not by itself separate time scales: two identical undamped oscillators coupled with stiffness k have normal modes at ω₀ and √(ω₀² + 2k), nearly equal when k ≪ ω₀², and neither decays; separation comes where the coupling dissipates relative differences faster than collective ones, as in ẋ = −ax − k(x − y), ẏ = −ay − k(y − x), whose collective and relative modes relax at rates a and a + 2k, and in a Laplacian flow ẋ = −κLx, where the spectrum of L sets the rates | The answer A20, A21 and A23 gave to the owner's conjecture at U20 that coupling necessarily induces scale separation ([CLAIM-473](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-473.md)). Two small computations: conservative coupling splits modes without separating or damping them, and dissipative coupling damps the relative mode at a rate that grows with the coupling. For a Laplacian flow the kernel is exact compatibility and the nonzero spectrum is the hierarchy of relaxation rates, so a spectral gap is where the separation comes from. Conceded, so Active. It gives a mechanism for [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)'s second half and is not a test of individuality. | Active |
| [CLAIM-482](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-482.md) v2 | An organization's aggregate revealed preference exists exactly when its record of winning moves never cycles, and where it exists it is fitted to one regime of authority, so an intervention on authority that changes the winning moves changes the fitted preference and the preference does not predict the change | The status review of 2026-10-27 ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)) found the record's later formal work bearing on an objection it never cited. [CLAIM-089](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-089.md)'s aggregate version says Northstar "simply prefers speed": the governing relations are the organization's revealed preference. [CLAIM-434](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-434.md), Active and demonstrated, says when such a preference exists: an ordering that every winning move climbs exists exactly when the wins never cycle. So the objection is not refuted in general. It is true of an organization whose record is acyclic, and unavailable for one whose record cycles. Where it holds, the ordering is read off the wins under one regime of authority. [CASE-003](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-003.md) changes authority and holds attitudes and evidence fixed, and the wins change. Then the fitted ordering changes too, and nothing in the first ordering predicted the second. The revealed preference redescribes the outcome of the governing relations, which is the reading [CLAIM-027](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-027.md)'s defeater excludes ("whose content predicts the outcome"). | Active |
| [CLAIM-485](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-485.md) v2 | In the self-governing sense, what endogenous governance adds over a behaviourally equivalent system with an external scheduler is not that it allocates authority among its own processes but that it can revise its own governing standards when they break down | The bridge the owner asked for on 2026-10-28, between Kahl's proposal (THEORY-1165), which is about agency in the sense that bears on responsibility, and [QUESTION-092](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-092.md), which fixes [TERM-045](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s sense 5, self-governing. It is the record's answer to the question. Internal allocation of authority, the second of [CLAIM-025](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md)'s separable capacities (governing among regimes), coordinates execution and does not make a system govern itself more than an external scheduler would. The capacity to revise its governing standards when they break down does: the third capacity, which [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) names as taking part in governing the conditions of its own transformation. Two systems matched within a regime differ under it, and they diverge in behaviour once that regime breaks down. | Active |
| [CLAIM-488](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-488.md) v3 | Le Cam deficiency, after Torgersen, would quantify the approximate case of the Blackwell order for translation, and decoder-only audience knowledge would make the coding problem a Wyner-Ziv problem | The two steps of the manuscript's §5 that [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md) carried until the status review of 2026-10-28 and that rest on works the record has not read: deficiency for the approximate case (Torgersen) and the Wyner-Ziv form of decoder side information. Split off when [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md) was narrowed to what its read sources support ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s third ruling). | Active |
| [CLAIM-492](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-492.md) v2 | If the self is defined to include whatever an agent cares about, the claim that all motivation serves the self is true by definition and rules nothing out; the thesis has content only with a criterion of the self's extent that can come apart from what the agent cares about | The classic objection to psychological egoism (Butler; Sober and Wilson, [LIT-1683](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1683.md)), turned on the owner's thesis. "Every motive is my motive" is trivially true and does not make every motive self-interested. "My self includes whatever I care about" makes the thesis unfalsifiable. It is answered if the thesis names an independent criterion of the self's extent, such as overlap, fusion or salient self-categorization, and predicts that motivation follows that criterion and not caring alone. | Active |
| [CLAIM-495](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-495.md) | For an O(d)-valued connection on a connected graph, the assignments that meet every edge relation xᵢ = Tᵢⱼxⱼ form a space isomorphic to the vectors at one vertex fixed by every holonomy based there, which is the kernel of the connection Laplacian; for d = 1, and for U(1) phases, that space is all or nothing, but for d > 1 a connection whose loops are not trivial can still keep a subspace on which every loop is, so compatibility among local frames can be partial and graded by direction; and edge maps that do not commute can compose to a flat loop, so non-commutativity is not holonomy | From A2 and A3 of the exchange "Paper assessment" (2026-10-29), which drew it out of [LIT-1820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1820.md)'s O(d) setting against [THEORY-1082](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1082.md)'s U(1) one. The proof and the example are the record's, checked numerically. It is the zeroth cohomology of the connection sheaf, so standard, and it says nothing about which organizations have such transports. | Active |
| [CLAIM-496](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-496.md) | Agreement between routes of translation is a measure of coherence, not of fidelity, and the two are independent: a rendering that sends every source utterance to one output makes direct and relay transport agree exactly while a receiver who could tell a promise from a prediction with no error is left at chance, and two routes that keep the act and differ in register disagree completely while losing nothing the act-identification task needs | From A4 and A5 of the exchange "Paper assessment" (2026-10-29), where the assistant carried [LIT-1820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1820.md)'s comparison of alternative paths over to translation and then warned that "path agreement is a coherence criterion, not a fidelity criterion". The constructions are the record's. It does not say path discrepancy is uninformative: it says it measures something [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md)'s directed loss does not, and conversely. | Active |
| [CLAIM-497](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-497.md) v2 | A system's causes are found at the coarsest description whose interventions are unambiguous: a macro description is causally proportionate where it merges only micro states that intervention cannot tell apart, and no coarse-graining carries more causal information than the micro description it supervenes on | The record's position on causal emergence after [THEORY-787](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-787.md) was rejected. A coarse-graining can be the right causal description, but not by beating the micro. Under one intervention distribution at both levels, no coarse-graining of a transition carries more effective information than its micro ([THEORY-1167](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1167.md)). The ones that lose nothing are exactly causal feature learning's partitions, which merge only micro states with the same interventional effects ([THEORY-1169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1169.md)). The step from there to "the causes are found at the coarsest such description" is the record's own, in the sense of proportionality. It does not say the macro adds causal information. | Active |
| [CLAIM-501](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-501.md) v2 | Gutt's interpretive resemblance also predicts that judged pragmatic observables beat text similarity, so the central theses' defeat conditions cannot tell the thesis from a relevance-theoretic account either | Split from [CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md) by the nineteenth status review ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation) and promoted by the twenty-first, once Gutt's 1989 thesis (LIT-1845) was read. [CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md) holds that functional equivalence and a proposition with its force both predict a pass on the central defeat test. This claim adds Gutt's relevance-theoretic account. The book ([LIT-784](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-784.md)) stays unread. | Active |
| [CLAIM-502](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-502.md) v2 | Multi-hop delegation can keep an operator's authority exactly independent of its own grants: under leave-one-out damped delegation, which counts the authority reaching each operator only along paths that have not already passed through it, an operator's grants raise the authority of every operator its grantee reaches and leave its own unchanged | A construction that shows [CLAIM-282](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md)'s old title false. Compute each operator's authority from A2's damped recursive rule with that operator's own outgoing grants removed. Then authority reaches it along paths of any length, but only along paths that have not passed through it, so nothing it grants can return to it. Its authority is exactly independent of its own grants, and a grant moves authority two hops and more. It does not say the rule conserves authority, that it closes the social route of moving others' grants, or that [CLAIM-375](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-375.md)'s guarantee carries over. | Active |
| [CLAIM-503](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-503.md) | Over finitely many states and finite outcome sets, one experiment is ε-deficient relative to another in every decision problem with losses in [0, 1] exactly when a single Markov kernel brings it within ε in total variation at every state, so the deficiency computed as a linear programme is the least such ε | Le Cam's randomization criterion for finite experiments, uniform in the state, with losses in [0, 1]. The least ε for which some kernel brings M within ε of N in total variation at every state, which [CLAIM-381](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-381.md) computes as a linear programme, equals the least ε for which M is ε-deficient relative to N in every finite decision problem. One direction composes N's rule with the kernel; the other is one minimax step over a bilinear objective. At ε = 0 it is the finite Blackwell order ([THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-506](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-506.md) v2 | The split of the last eukaryotic common ancestor's central carbon metabolism, archaeal enzymes in the cytosol and alphaproteobacterial ones in the mitochondrion, does not single out syntrophy: a host that kept its own archaeal glycolysis and took up a bacterium with a TCA cycle leaves it whether the partnership began in syntrophy or by engulfment by an already complex host, and what the split counts against is a host whose carbon metabolism was replaced by the symbiont's | Split from [THEORY-1109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1109.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation). [THEORY-1109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1109.md) reports what Santana-Molina and colleagues find and that they read it as support for syntrophy; this claim is the record's judgement that the split cannot carry that reading. | Active |
| [CLAIM-508](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-508.md) v2 | Gene ancestries alone cannot tell a symbiotic partner from a source of transferred genes: a partner whose genes were mostly lost, replaced or spread thin would leave the diffuse trace that Tobiasson and colleagues read as piecemeal transfer, and Bernabeu and colleagues concede that their donor signals say nothing of the kind of interaction | Split from [THEORY-1104](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1104.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation). [THEORY-1104](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1104.md) reports Tobiasson and colleagues' reading of diffuse bacterial genes as transfer; [THEORY-1105](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1105.md) reports Bernabeu and colleagues' concession about their own donors. This claim is what the record draws from both. | Active |
| [CLAIM-509](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-509.md) v2 | Stem lengths alone do not establish an order of acquisition in eukaryogenesis, neither Pittis and Gabaldón's late mitochondrion nor Bernabeu and colleagues' transfer waves: normalized stem length measures time only if rates before and after LECA are proportional, it shortens as closer relatives are sampled, the alphaproteobacterial separation from other bacteria rests on P = 0.044, and on Tobiasson and colleagues' data it does not behave as a clock | Split from [THEORY-1102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1102.md) and [THEORY-1101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1101.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation). The two readings, now Active, report what the papers find; this claim is the record's judgement of what stem lengths can establish. | Active |
| [CLAIM-512](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-512.md) v4 | The diachronic thesis faces two objections: a dilemma, that read narrowly it fails for judgments not about any organization's continuation, such as that suffering is bad, and read broadly every judgment is met vacuously as a preference between continuations unless the organizational description adds causal specificity, transfer or counterfactual discrimination; and a distinction, that evaluating a history is not prescribing its continuation, so a judgment can be determinate with no future transformation fixed | The objection to [CLAIM-518](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md), put by the assistant itself in A26 §6 and A27 §10 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): "If we call every difference between possible worlds a change in some organization, then all normative judgments can be represented in these terms without learning much", and "A judgment that suffering is bad, for instance, is not obviously about organizational persistence". Conceded by CLAIM-518 at its versions 2 and 3. Its broad horn is the condition CLAIM-608 must meet. A27's three tests are the form an answer would take. | Active |
| [CLAIM-513](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-513.md) | Across a family of goals, a world model is not an optional explanation of competent behaviour: in a fully observed, finite, communicating, stationary environment, a goal-conditioned policy within a factor 1 − δ of optimal on every composite goal of depth n fixes every transition probability to within √(2P(1 − P)/((n − 1)(1 − δ))), so observers reading the same policy must ascribe the same world model; what it leaves open is whether a predictive component is realized inside the agent, since a lookup table over histories and goals has the same policy | From the reading of Richens, Abel, Bellot and Everitt ([LIT-1891](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1891.md), [NOTE-1469](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1469.md)), registered as the objection to watch against the owner's U20 thesis [CLAIM-519](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md). It defeats that thesis's functional reading only. The thesis's defeated_if is not met: the theorem holds "regardless of ... architecture", makes no matched-resource comparison and no intervention on internals, and its authors say the map runs "from the agent's policy rather than its activations". Within its scope, though, calling a world model an explanatory attribution is too weak. The bound was re-derived and checked against an adversarial agent. | Active |
| [CLAIM-515](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md) v2 | Whether an organization has a cognitive property is four questions, not one: what information about the property can be recovered from its behaviour, what capabilities it can actually exercise, what mechanisms realize them, and whether it can maintain or transform those mechanisms; the four can come apart, and none should be silently substituted for another | The general principle the owner drew at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): "When asking whether an organization 'has' a cognitive property, distinguish the information recoverable from its behavior, the capabilities it can actually exercise, the mechanisms realizing those capabilities, and its ability to maintain or transform those mechanisms." It was drawn from the world-model case ([CLAIM-514](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md)) and judged "sufficiently general—and sufficiently testable—that it deserves an explicit place in Nucleation's research program". Interpretive: its instances are demonstrated case by case, and the generalization is not. | Active |
| [CLAIM-516](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-516.md) | Where every constraint capacity turns over at a positive rate and is produced only by others, with no basal production and production vanishing as its producers do, capacities whose production graph is acyclic all decay to zero: a capacity that persists needs a productive cycle among its ancestors, and removing a feedback edge set extinguishes every capacity; a cycle is necessary and not sufficient, and a one-member cycle is not closure | From A10 §1 and §5A of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), after the owner's "try to progress the theoretical program". The proof was rechecked by the reader of U7–U10. It is known in substance from autocatalytic-set theory, as A10 said. What it adds to the record is the boundary with closure: the necessary cycle may be a self-loop, and a self-loop is not closure in [TERM-070](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-070.md)'s sense or [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md)'s, which need two or more constraints. | Active |
| [CLAIM-517](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-517.md) | A successor regulator keeps a viable set positively invariant if, at every boundary context, its response distribution is within γ/L in total variation of a regulator that certifies inward margin γ, the dynamics being L-Lipschitz in that distribution; an average distillation loss certifies this only through coverage of the boundary contexts, so fidelity measured in ordinary operation certifies nothing about viability | From A16 §4 and §5 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), the owner having quoted its conclusion at U17: "preserving a regulator's response distribution sufficiently accurately can guarantee preservation of a physical organization's viability". The algebra was rechecked; the regularity conditions A16 left implicit are stated here. A16's application to its own construction (γ = 0.16) was notional, since that model has no regulator distribution and L is undefined there. | Active |
| [CLAIM-518](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md) v3 | Normative judgments about an organization's continuity, reform or obligations can depend on diachronic relations that descriptions of present states or terminal outcomes do not show, so specifying the relevant relations and histories can be necessary to apply them adequately; which continuations ought to follow is a further normative question, not a prerequisite of every normative judgment | From the owner's observation at U26 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), "normative judgements are only cognizable when they are relative to a judgement of whether some organization should persist or change", as narrowed at the owner's review the same day. What survives is that judgments about continuity, reform and obligation can need histories that present states and outcomes do not show. What is dropped is that every judgment needs a prescribed future: evaluating a history and fixing the admissible continuations are different problems. "Cognizable" is read as "well-defined", [CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md)'s sense. Its objection, CLAIM-512, is conceded whole: the narrow horn and the distinction at version 2, the broad horn at version 3. The clause the broad horn removed, that the diachronic relations add to CLAIM-363's relata, is CLAIM-608. | Active |
| [CLAIM-520](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-520.md) v2 | The value of keeping a corrective capacity is conditional on objectives, uncertainty and cost: a free, optional audit cannot lower a single time-consistent decision-maker's expected performance, but an audit that costs C to maintain and bears on k decisions with error rate ε is worth k(0.25 − 0.5ε) − C in the exchange's model, negative when C is large or k small, and where no hypothesis fits the world, correction gains no reward and improves only calibration | From A24 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), answering the owner's U24 question whether corrigibility's desirability had been established. The arithmetic was rechecked by the turns' reader. This is the subject-matter half of the answer. The support half, that the record's constructions do not establish that corrigibility ought to be kept, is [ARG-042](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-042.md), which this claim undercuts. | Active |
| [CLAIM-521](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-521.md) | An organization's present coupling strength need not reveal the stability of the process maintaining it: in a constructed system whose maintained connector and capacities set a three-unit coupling, the recovery rate of the maintenance goes to zero at its saddle-node while the coupling's spectral gap there stays near 0.989 | From A12 §6 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), which called it "a surprising result". It is generic for any saddle-node whose fold sits away from zero with no feedback from the coupled units to the maintaining core, so it is built in rather than surprising. It is filed because it is a construction [QUESTION-125](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-125.md) asks for: one in which the regime changes while the block's gap does not. All numbers were recomputed. | Active |
| [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) v2 | Recovery under interventions on state cannot show where maintenance is realized: an outside controller that measures the constraint capacities and supplies the internal production law as state feedback yields the same trajectory under every perturbation of state, damage and recovery included, even with every capacity observed exactly; only interventions on the production mechanisms, relative to a declared boundary, separate the two | From A10 §4 (its Proposition 5) of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). Close to definitional, and checked: substituting the controller gives the same differential equation. It extends [CLAIM-414](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md) from passive observation to every intervention on state. As the reader noted, the causal dependence among the capacities is the same in both systems; only where the mechanism sits relative to the boundary differs, which is [CLAIM-194](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md)'s point about boundaries. | Active |
| [CLAIM-523](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md) v2 | For a normatively relevant discrepancy to change what an organization does, three distinct achievements are needed and any can fail while the others hold: legibility, by which the discrepancy becomes recognizable; volitional efficacy, by which a corresponding demand can move action; and correctability, by which a fitting revision can be carried out within deadline and resources; none establishes that the demand or the revision is justified, and whether the norm-satisfying histories the agent can still realize are empty depends partly on what its earlier actions destroyed | The owner's synthesis at review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). It was first filed as a dated note on [QUESTION-364](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-364.md), and filed as a claim at the owner's word ("this should probably be a new CLAIM, not hidden inside the prose of a QUESTION"). It joins three held entries, legibility ([TERM-064](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md)), will-organization ([TERM-023](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-023.md)) and correctability ([TERM-085](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-085.md)), into one account of normative efficacy. It extends [CLAIM-349](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-349.md)'s split of access, authority and action from an organization's own signals to normatively relevant discrepancies. Proposed: the separations are argued, not built. | Active |
| [CLAIM-524](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-524.md) | Whether functionally equivalent realizations are connected depends on which paths are admissible: for f = u₁v₁ + u₂v₂ with nonnegative weights, (1, 1, 0, 0) and (0, 0, 1, 1) are joined by a curve along which f stays 1 though the straight line between them falls to ½, and under any resource budget below √2 times the endpoints' cost no path with f = 1 joins them | From the owner's remark at U17 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), that the reconstruction fibres "reminds me of loss landscape connected mode stuff (which might just be a consequence of high dimensional geometry? ... probably already discussed on the nucleation record)". It is: see below. A17 §9 gave the curve and A18 §7 the budget for a tied-weight family; the general bound here is the reader's, rechecked. "Viable mode connectivity" is A18's name and is not filed as a term. | Active |
| [CLAIM-525](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-525.md) v2 | Information in the sense the Simondonian readings give it, a disparity whose resolution reorders the system that takes it up, is in the line's terms a change in the interpreter or in the questions receivers can decide, not evidence about a fixed situation, so Blackwell's order leaves it out by construction and the two accounts are not rivals | The record's placing, on 2026-10-31, of the information concept in the Simondon readings (Iliadis 2013; Bencherki and Iliadis 2021; Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy 2024) against the line's Blackwell treatment. The readings' information is what reorders a receiving system; the line's is evidence about a fixed situation for a fixed receiver. The first falls in the line's interpreter channel and change of cover. It gives the readings an operational test of failing to inform, which they lack. It does not say Simondon rejects the quantitative theory, and it is not Simondon's mapping: his text is unread here. | Active |
| [CLAIM-526](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-526.md) v2 | Describing persons and organizations as coexisting levels of one process removes the question of how already-constituted agents add up to a collective, but not the question of levels: whether a collective variable has dynamics of its own, closed against the activity that realizes it, can be decided on a process description that presupposes no agents, is sometimes decided no, and a closed collective variable can be an aggregate that coexists with its realization while keeping none of its members' distinctions | Filed on reading Bencherki & Iliadis 2021 and Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy 2024, who hold that the "scaling up" problem "vanishes the moment communication is viewed eventfully" ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), p. 1364) because persons and organizations are "different informational levels that preserve all the characteristics of their organized components" ([LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md), ms. p. 21, proposition 2). The record's closure results show what survives. What vanishes is the picture of agents adding up. What remains is whether a higher variable runs on its own, which is a question about variables and is decidable. The record's own case of a closed collective variable is a sum, an aggregate, that coexists with its units, so "stages or coexisting levels" is not a dichotomy. It does not say that the agent picture is right, or that organizations are aggregates of members. | Active |
| [CLAIM-528](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-528.md) v2 | That a mechanism realizes a capacity can mean that the capacity is produced through it over time or that the capacity consists in it at a time, and interventions show only the first: a pathway whose disabling changes the capacity after a delay is a cause, can be intervened on surgically, and can be located relative to a declared boundary, whereas every intervention on a capacity that consists in its parts also changes some part along another path, so that relation is underdetermined by intervention data and is inferred by abduction or from simultaneity and settled parthood; and which of the two a given dependence is depends on the time resolution at which a description treats the parts' response as instantaneous | Filed on reading the fat-handedness debate after Craver: Baumgartner & Gebharter 2016, Baumgartner & Casini 2017 and Baumgartner, Casini & Krickel 2020. It says what their result does and does not reach in the record. [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s conclusion is causal and is left standing; [CLAIM-515](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md)'s "realized", read synchronically, is not shown by discriminating interventions; and the debate's own line between causation and constitution, simultaneity, moves with the time scale, as [CLAIM-480](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md)'s chain shows. It does not say that constitution is unknowable, or that the record's organizations have constituents in the mechanists' sense. | Active |
| [CLAIM-529](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-529.md) v3 | An organization can be individuated without presupposing it as a declared candidate whose verdict can come out false: criteria stated on the candidate's interactions (whether benefit can be booked per member, which interactions the others depend on, what removing an interaction type does, whether its order survives release from an outside scaffold) apply to a grouping not yet assumed to be a unit, while criteria stated as members' attitudes toward the group (a goal about it, belonging, identity) make it partly constituted by being taken as one, individuating it by a different relation, unavailable where members have no such attitudes | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)). Their abstract says transitions in individuality are hard to describe without circularity, since the features used are products of the transition, and claims a non-circular description that the body never argues. The body holds the parts of an answer, and they are of two kinds. Criteria on interactions (per-member accounting of benefit, entrenchment order, knockout of interaction types, release from a scaffold) can test a declared candidate without assuming it is a unit ([CLAIM-405](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md)), and the scaffold test needs the declared boundary ([CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)). Criteria on members' attitudes toward the group (shared goal, belonging, focal goal of sustaining it) individuate constitutively, which is not the non-circular route and is unavailable for organisms without such attitudes. It does not say the paper argues this, and it leaves the presupposed lower-level units where the paper leaves them. | Active |
| [CLAIM-530](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-530.md) v2 | Where maintenance is realized is a question of constitutive relevance only through its parthood condition: an internal producer and an outside controller supplying the same production law as state feedback meet mutual manipulability's two manipulability conditions identically, since disabling or stimulating either changes the maintained capacities and intervening on the capacities changes the activity of either, so what puts one inside and the other outside is parthood, a boundary the experiments presuppose and do not find | The record's join of [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) with the mechanist account of constitution, from Craver and Bechtel's admission that interlevel experiments are symmetrical and show componency only prima facie ([THEORY-1287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1287.md)). In [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s pair the bottom-up and top-down interventions come out alike for producer and controller. So the criterion separates them only by its parthood clause, which is [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s declared boundary. The criterion is cited as Baumgartner and Gebharter state it (LIT-1934, p. 8, read in full in NOTE-1493); Craver's own texts stay unread. It does not say no criterion can draw the boundary. Closure, a producer that is itself maintained by what it produces, is a candidate that [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s one-variable model cannot express. | Active |
| [CLAIM-531](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-531.md) v2 | Generative entrenchment does not by itself give organizational closure: an entrenched core, which later interactions depend on so that perturbing it is catastrophic and perturbing them tolerable, can sit at the root of an acyclic dependency order, and where interactions turn over such an order persists only while something outside supplies its core; an organization that is both entrenched and closed has a core containing a cycle of mutual maintenance, each interaction on which is itself core unless its share of the maintenance is redundant | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)), who mark the step from conexus to community by generative entrenchment of core interactions and then, with "Hence", by organizational closure. It does not say their communities lack closure, only that entrenchment and knockout do not show it; and it reads Wimsatt's concept only as they quote it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-532](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-532.md) v2 | Self-formation, in the sense the record holds (the transformation dimension of a will-organization), is the production by an agent's own activity on a discrepancy it cannot yet resolve of a maintained capacity, a new distinction it can make legible or a new channel by which it can act, that outlasts the discrepancy and serves a class of later ones; it is told apart from learning an action by transfer to discrepancies of the same class after the inducing conditions are gone, and from a capacity installed or upheld from outside by interventions on the processes that produce and maintain it | The positive account A33 §7 offered, at the owner's U33 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), sharpened by the reader of U32–U33 so that it can fail. The steps A33 chains, discrepancy to discrimination to response to maintained capacity to revised governance, are not a sequence ([CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) v5 | The sensitivity that formal chaos gives a will's dynamics is not control over them: in Kane's self-forming actions, chaotic amplification keeps the outcome open, but it magnifies the agent's efforts, uncontrolled fluctuations and outside inputs alike, so what would make the outcome the agent's is how its own control couples to the amplifying directions, relative to noise and to other parties' inputs and with what feedback, which sensitivity does not supply; and under weak noise what amplification touches lasts only where it reaches the slow modes | The owner's, at U16 and U20 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02). | [CLAIM-534](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-534.md) v2 | A plural will's motivational integration, a dimension of freedom of will the record names and leaves unanalysed, is the extent to which the demands it maintains are jointly met, within tolerances it can recognize, across the contexts where they interact, and kept so under its own dynamics; it is neither agreement among the demands nor the dominance of one, and its parts come apart: realizability (the tolerance frontier), realization (governance frustration), maintenance (viability) and the allocation of the tolerance each demand gives up | A positive account, filed at the owner's U33 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02): "are there any positive accounts or even just hypotheses we should consider documenting on the record (even if just as proposals)?" | [CLAIM-535](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-535.md) | An organization that acts on what it observes has a policy acceptable in every circumstance exactly when, for each observation, the circumstances it cannot tell apart share an acceptable action; so every circumstance having an acceptable action does not give a policy, a finer observation never removes one, and where acceptable actions overlap the coarsest observations that suffice are several and incomparable, so which distinctions must be made legible depends on which acceptable action the organization commits to | A33 §4 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), at the owner's U33 request for positive accounts, with A30 §2's example and A32's Claim B. | [CLAIM-536](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-536.md) | A categorical model of perspectives and an LDA-style model differ in where the mixture lives: the first draws every act's perspective from one fixed categorical distribution, the second gives each episode its own mixture, drawn from a Dirichlet, and draws each act from it; the Dirichlet is a distribution over mixtures, not the perspectives themselves, and with symmetric concentration a over K perspectives two acts in one episode share a perspective with probability (a + 1)/(Ka + 1) against 1/K across episodes, so the concentration runs from one perspective per episode, as in persona selection (a → 0), to a fresh independent draw for every act (a → ∞) | The owner's U12 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), stated precisely: "H1 isn't LDA like though. that's my point. it's a categorical distribution. the topics in H@ are the dirichlet distribution which parameterizes the categorical distribution, which is what distinguishes H2 from H1 and why H2 is an LDA." | [CLAIM-537](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-537.md) | In tolerance-bounded compatibility on a graph with disturbed offsets, \|Dx − a₀ − w\| ≤ δ for \|w_e\| ≤ η_e, a compatible configuration exists for every disturbance exactly when \|cᵀa₀\| + Σ η_e\|c_e\| ≤ Σ δ_e\|c_e\| on every cycle, and one configuration serves every disturbance exactly when η ≤ δ and \|cᵀa₀\| ≤ Σ(δ_e − η_e)\|c_e\|; an agent that chooses its configuration from what it observes needs the second condition within each class of disturbances it cannot tell apart, so whether a compatible state can be selected lies between the two and depends on what the agent can read | A30 §§2–3 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), at the owner's "keep going", with the second and third conditions derived by the reader of U30–U31 and checked by simulation (500 random instances, no mismatch). | [CLAIM-538](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-538.md) | On a finite graph of contexts whose overlaps carry preferred real offsets a and tolerances δ_e ≥ 0, an assignment within every tolerance, \|Dx − a\| ≤ δ, exists exactly when no cycle's holonomy exceeds the sum of its tolerances; with every δ_e > 0 the least uniform enlargement of the tolerances that admits one is the largest ratio, over simple cycles, of holonomy to summed tolerance, so the obstruction is certified by a cycle; the feasible allocations of tolerance depend on the offsets only through their class in H¹, so local adjustment can move a mismatch among the overlaps of a cycle and never remove it; and an evaluation that omits one overlap of every witnessing cycle reports a compatibility that does not hold | The owner's U27 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), "compatibility of tolerance bounds", with U28's pointer to the record's sheaf tools, worked out at A28 §3 and A29 §§3–4, 7 and A32's Claim A. Checked by linear programming against brute-force cycle enumeration on random graphs. | Active |
| [CLAIM-539](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-539.md) v2 | Jennings's attention as the source of a free will has Frankfurt's two-level architecture with its upper level changed from an attitude to a process: the whole collection of an agent's interests, prioritizing, settles which first-order interest becomes effective, as a second-order volition does for Frankfurt, but by metacontrol and not by endorsement; so it inherits unchanged the objection that a manipulated organization can meet the condition, and what it adds to Frankfurt is that the process forms new interests and is a contextually emergent cause | The owner's U14 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02): "would it be fair to say Jennings theory is Frankfurt with a hat on?" | [CLAIM-542](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-542.md) v2 | Sensitivity does not fix the allocation or the authorship of control: linearized, every input reaches the final state through the same transition operator, ∂x_T/∂w_t = Φ(T, t)B_w(t), so systems with the same Lyapunov spectrum can differ arbitrarily in what an agent's own channel, an outside party's channel and noise each reach and at what least energy; and along one unstable direction a larger exponent λ lowers the least effort to reach a displacement, since W_T = b²(e^{2λT} − 1)/2λ grows with λ, while a constant open-loop input against white noise entering the same direction has terminal signal-to-noise ratio tending to (bu/σ)√(2/λ), which falls as λ grows, so only feedback that observes the state turns cheaper control into reliable direction | The demonstrated part of the owner's U16 and U20 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), "controllability vs sensitivity". | [CLAIM-543](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-543.md) v3 | What separates a language model's distribution over personas from a distribution over organizational perspectives is not whether the latent model is hierarchical, since a mixture or an LDA-style admixture already is, but whether some latent components condition which others are available or consequential: a model whose components are exchangeable given their weights is organizationally flat however many levels its prior has, and dependencies among components count as organization (organization as relational arrangement) only where interventions, not fit, support them | The owner's U8 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02): "think of the relations as bayesian hierarchy, so H1 is a flat plate model and H2 has hierarchical/causal structure", said of a language model read as a distribution over perspectives under the Persona Selection Model (U6). | [CLAIM-546](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-546.md) v2 | Negative frequency dependence that keeps two types in coexistence does not make their interaction cooperative: in Hawk–Dove with cost C above value V each type increases when rare and they coexist at the interior equilibrium of V/C Hawks, with Hawks still taking the whole resource from Doves, and on the Black Queen account producers of a leaked good and the cells that use it without paying coexist at a frequency set by the community's need; so whether types persist together and whether they cooperate are separate questions, and a coexistence criterion answers only the first | From §3 of the synthesis "The Evolution of Cooperation: From Coexistence to Symbiosis to Morality", which the owner supplied on 2026-11-04: "stable coexistence of strategies is not necessarily the same as stable cooperation: cooperators and defectors can coexist without eliminating exploitation". | [CLAIM-547](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-547.md) v2 | Cooperation within groups and the coexistence of groups are distinct targets that can trade off: in the group-selection rule of Nowak's five, b/c > 1 + n/m, cooperation spreads because a group that grows to size n splits and another group is driven extinct, so the mechanism that stabilizes cooperation inside groups works by removing groups; cooperation local to a group, the persistence of several groups whose interests are opposed, and concern for those outside one's group are three achievements, and none of them secures the next | From §7 of the synthesis "The Evolution of Cooperation: From Coexistence to Symbiosis to Morality", which the owner supplied on 2026-11-04. | [CLAIM-556](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-556.md) v2 | Before the four obstructions to a transition stands a failure of compatibility, no configuration meeting the demands, repaired by changing the constraints, since dropping a demand is not relief; and after them a failure of regeneration, the capability not surviving turnover, repaired by maintenance or reproduction; so a diagnosis runs through six levels, each with its own repair | A's proposal, from the pasted synthesis on resource-bounded realizability (three responses, pasted by the owner on 2026-11-05, continuing the exchange on constraint architectures), Response 2 §3: a six-level diagnostic hierarchy, compatibility, reachability, affordability, controllability, reliability and regeneration, each with what repairs it.
